text:
Clayton Keller's season reads like a passer's diary. The Mammoth captain has 29 points in 24 games and 24 of them are assists; 19 have come on the power play, which runs through him. He just came back into the lineup in Winnipeg after missing time, alongside Dylan Guenther.

The goals are the odd part: five on 7.7 expected. He keeps getting looks, and goals tend to follow chances. The five-on-five picture is the real worry. Utah's share of expected goals is 9.5 points worse with Keller on the ice than off it, a sharp turn for a player Evolving-Hockey had sixth among all forwards in wins above replacement last season. All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) still rates his playmaking at the 98th percentile, so the creativity hasn't gone anywhere. Our range projects 83 to 110 points, which says the power play will keep feeding him. Whether he can tilt even-strength play again is the thing to watch.
